data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'esh', meaning fire or ash. The name Asher signifies the one who brings happiness or blessings. The name Asher carries the meaning “Ash, or the one who brings happiness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asher usually hope their child will grow to embody ash, or the one who brings happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: Asir ibn Hisham Al-Asadi, known as Asir Al-Khuzai or Asher ibn Hazrat, was a Persian poet who lived during the Abbasid Caliphate. He is famous for his panegyric poetry in praise of the caliphs and their courts. Asher's most famous work is the 'Diwan Asheri', a collection of poems primarily focused on the caliphs Al-Mansur and Al-Mamun.

historical_references.context: Asher or Asir is also the name of a Persian tribe mentioned in early Islamic sources. They lived in the region of Asir in Arabia, which is now part of modern-day Saudi Arabia. During the early Islamic period, the Asher tribe played a significant role in the military and political landscape, and their leaders sometimes held positions of power within the Umayyad Caliphate.
